narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 68.7% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt; that means failure was judged substantially more likely than passing based on the profile reviewed. The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you are in the lowest decile, compared with an average of about the sixth decile among accepted students. That very low third-year rank pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing was the second-strongest factor, also lowest decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth decile, and it pushed in the same direction. Your LSAT score of 38 was the third most influential factor; it is slightly above the accepted-student average of 37.18, so it counted in your favor and pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to overcome the academic-standing concerns. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 is also above the accepted average and likely helped, though it was not among the top drivers. To strengthen a future application, focus on raising your academic record, especially any remaining or repeatable coursework, seek advising about how to explain your class rank, and build evidence of bar-exam readiness. You may also consider retaking the LSAT only if a meaningful score increase is realistic, and consult admissions staff about whether postponing or completing additional preparation would improve your chances.
